items.item_text: Basic Life Support required at hire
Nurse Midwife National Certification required at hire
Drug Enforcement Administration Registration required at hire
Registered Nurse License (California) required at hire
Certified Nurse Midwife (California) required at hire
Masters degree in Nursing (MSN) AND minimum four (4) years of experience in nurse-midwifery.
MBA or Masters in Health Care Administration.
Minimum three (3) years of experience in a leadership role with or without direct reports.
Provides developmental opportunities for others; builds collaborative, cross-functional relationships.
Solicits and acts on performance feedback; works closely with employees to set goals and provide open feedback and coaching to drive performance improvement.
Pursues professional growth; develops and provides training and development to talent for growth opportunities; supports execution of performance management guidelines and expectations.
Leads, adapts, implements, and stays up to date with organizational change, challenges, feedback, best practices, processes, and industry trends.
Fosters open dialogue amongst team members, engages, motivates, and promotes collaboration within and across teams.
Delegates tasks and decisions as appropriate; provides appropriate support, guidance, and scope; encourages development and consideration of options in decision making.

Manages designated work unit or team by translating business plans into tactical action items; oversees the completion of work assignments and identifies opportunities for improvement; ensures all policies and procedures are followed.

Aligns team efforts; builds accountability for and measuring progress in achieving results; determines and ensures processes and methodologies are implemented; resolves escalated issues as appropriate; sets standards and measures progress.
Fosters the development of work plans to meet business priorities and deadlines; obtains and distributes resources.

Removes obstacles that impact performance; identifies and addresses improvement opportunities; guides performance and develops contingency plans accordingly; influences teams to execute in alignment with operational objectives.

Guides regulatory compliance and quality improvement efforts by: collaborating with department leadership to ensure adherence to The Joint Commission (TJC) standards, state and federal regulations, and accreditation requirements; advocating for patient safety by proactively identifying and addressing potential risks in clinical care processes and partnering with senior leaders to implement risk prevention strategies; participating in audits and inspections, and overseeing documentation systems to ensure readiness for regulatory reporting and reviews; leading the development, implementation, and evaluation of quality improvement initiatives aimed at enhancing maternal and neonatal outcomes; and may include conducting peer review as directed.

Provides and manages comprehensive midwifery care by: conducting examinations and delivering care services across the prenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, and gynecological stages; collaborating with cross-functional health care providers to aid complex pregnancies and cases; educating patients and family members to promote understanding and engagement in the care process; modeling culturally competent and patient-centered care tailored to meet the diverse needs, values, and preferences of individuals and families; and identifying and implementing evidence-based protocols and staying current with advancements in midwifery to lead efforts for standardizing care and continuously improving patient outcomes.

Manages nurse midwifery services and operations by: leading the recruitment, onboarding, and retention of midwifery team members; evaluating clinic and patient appointment demands to develop and approve schedules that ensure appropriate staffing, clinic access, and continuous in-patient care; developing and implementing policies and performance standards to drive operational efficiency and continuity of care across the department; organizing agendas and leading team meetings to address operational updates, clinical developments, and team performance; facilitating and advocating for the cross-functional integration of nurse-midwifery functions to enhance care delivery; assisting in budget planning and resource allocation with senior leaders to optimize financial performance and support quality care strategies; and developing, monitoring, and analyzing performance metrics to recommend areas for operational improvement and ensure alignment with department goals.

Manages the professional development of midwifery staff by: mentoring, training, and identifying and providing access to continuing education opportunities for staff and/or family practice or OBGYN residents where applicable; encouraging participation in case discussions to foster a culture of learning and continuous improvement; promoting midwifery care through the strategic planning and development of community outreach programs, workshops, and educational initiatives; and may include coordinating clinical rotations for midwifery students from accredited programs.
National Provider Identifier required at hire
Nurse Midwife Furnishing Number (California) required at hire
